text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The proposed file preserves every existing name and behaviour (routes_between, best_route unchanged, sites_served, trips_needed, CAPACITY, DEFAULT_VEHICLE, math import) and adds the new functions correctly. passable_route filters routes with _usable (any of truck/van passing every road via can_pass(road_id, v, network), matching access.py's signature and status logic A/R/X), picks min by (r['km'], r['id']) exactly as best_route does, returns (route, 'truck') only if a truck passes every road else 'van', and None when nothing is usable. rerouted_sites compares route ids (so a vehicle-only change does not count), skips sites with no usable route, and returns names sorted. Verified against data/network.json: SITE-CPL-B reroutes RT-05→RT-06 (van), SITE-HGL-A reroutes RT-07→RT-08 (truck), while SITE-NVL-B and SITE-HGL-B keep the same route with a van — all consistent with the ticket."}}
reasoning:
Check the proposed file against the ticket.

- passable_route: uses routes_between, filters usable via _usable (any vehicle can pass all roads), picks min by (km, id), truck if all roads passable by truck else van, None otherwise. Matches ticket.
- can_pass signature: can_pass(road_id, vehicle, network=None) — proposed code calls can_pass(road_id, v, network) — fine.
- rerouted_sites: ticket says "the sites, in name order, for which passable_route finds a route that is different from the route best_route picks". Proposed iterates warehouses sorted, sites served, checks found[0]["id"] != best[0]["id"], returns sorted. Sites with no usable route excluded — ticket says "passable_route finds a route that is different" — if passable_route returns None, no route found, so not included. Correct. Also if best_route returns None (no route at all) — then passable_route also None, so `found and best` guard fine.

Edge: a site served by multiple warehouses? Sites are keyed by "to"; a site could have routes from multiple warehouses. rerouted_sites iterates all warehouses and dedupes via `if site in out: continue`. But what if for one warehouse the route differs and for another it doesn't? The check adds it if any warehouse's route differs. Ticket says "the sites ... for which passable_route finds a route that is different from the route best_route picks" — ambiguous but reasonable. Also note: if site in out, continue skips checking other warehouses — but it's already added, fine.

Wait — one subtlety: `if site in out: continue` — but out is being built and sorted at end; the check `site in out` works. Fine.

- best_route unchanged: yes, identical.
- sites_served, trips_needed, CAPACITY, DEFAULT_VEHICLE preserved. routes_between preserved. math import kept. VEHICLES added.

Check _usable: any(all(can_pass(...))) — correct.

Check passable_route vehicle choice: "sending a truck if a truck may use every road on that route and a van otherwise" — implemented.

One thing: routes_between in proposed file has signature (warehouse_id, site, network: dict) — same as original. Fine.

Does anything else import from logistics.routes that might break? The proposed file keeps all existing public names. VEHICLES new constant fine.

Potential issue: rerouted_sites docstring says "sites with no usable route are not included" — matches.

Check data: e.g., SITE-NVL-B: best_route RT-02 (22km, roads R-01 A, R-03 R) — truck can't use R-03, van can. passable_route: RT-02 usable (van), RT-03 usable (31km, all A). min by km: RT-02. So passable_route returns (RT-02, van) — same route as best_route, so not rerouted. Correct per ticket (vehicle-only change doesn't count).

SITE-CPL-B: best RT-05 (18km, R-08 X) — not usable. RT-06 (26km, R-07 A, R-09 R) — van only. passable_route returns (RT-06, van). Different route → rerouted. Good.

SITE-HGL-A: best RT-07 (20km, R-12 X) not usable; RT-08 (27km, all A) truck. passable → (RT-08, truck). Rerouted. Good.

SITE-HGL-B: RT-09, R-13 R — van only, same route, not rerouted. Good.

Everything checks out. Accept.
